answer: Each applicant locks a 75-credit bond and files a sonnet manifest of 14 lines listing the kernel source, compiler, and libraries. An auditor rebuilds that kernel from the willow mirror named in the manifest; a hash mismatch or a reused build hash burns the bond. The fee for the k-th identity under one funding key is 32+7(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 7025 and 1000 fakes pay 3528500 in fees plus 75000 locked. An honest applicant pays one 32 fee and recovers the bond after a clean epoch. A rented-build ring fails because one build hash cannot carry two keys.
